cd /tmp/xhs-c6-host-u3y4tsnw; git status --short; git add -A && git commit -q -m "s2: add Encode/Decode for ShapeIndex

Serialize a ShapeIndex together with all of its shapes and its full
spatial cell structure so it can be loaded without rebuilding. Shape IDs
(including gaps left by removed shapes) are preserved so cell references
stay valid. All built-in Shape types are supported. Encode applies any
pending updates first, and Decode validates its input, returning errors
for truncated, corrupted, or oversized data instead of panicking.

Also fix ShapeIndex issues that prevented a decoded (or previously built)
index from being updated:
- applyUpdatesInternal iterated to len(shapes) instead of nextID, so
  shapes were skipped once any shape had been removed.
- makeIndexCell used len(shapes) as its sentinel shape ID, which
  corrupted cells when shape IDs exceed the shape count.
- Incremental updates deadlocked (shrinkToFit/updateEdges re-entered
  maybeApplyUpdates) and removal was unimplemented; updates to a built

content.text:
`ShapeIndex` now has `Encode(io.Writer)` and `Decode(io.Reader)`. Everything is committed on a new branch, `shapeindex-encoding`, as commit `a8e9bb5`. There's no `main` branch in this checkout, only `master`, so I branched from `master` at the same commit. `go vet` is clean, the full test suite passes in the container, and a 60-second fuzz run of the decoder found no crashes.

**What it does** (new file `s2/shapeindex_encode.go`):
- **All built-in shape types round-trip:** `Polygon`, `Loop`, `Polyline`, `PointVector`, `LaxPolyline`, `LaxLoop` and `LaxPolygon`. Each comes back as the same type with identical edges and chains. Encoding any other shape type returns an error.
- **Shape IDs survive,** including gaps left by removed shapes, so cell references stay valid. Shapes added after decoding get new IDs that continue from where the original left off.
- **The full cell structure is saved.** A decoded index is ready to use: queries and iteration work without calling `Build`.
- **No `Build` needed before encoding:** `Encode` applies any pending changes first. An empty index still encodes to a few bytes, and zero-edge shapes (empty and full polygons and loops, empty polylines) and polygons with mixed loop counts, including empty loops, round-trip.
- **Bad input returns an error, never a panic.** Every count is capped and lists grow only as data is actually read, so a huge count in the input can't trigger a huge allocation. Cell IDs, shape IDs and edge IDs are all validated, and so are coordinate values. A recover guard catches anything missed. If decoding fails, the index is left unchanged.

**Existing bugs I had to fix in `s2/shapeindex.go`.** A decoded index is an already-built index, so adding shapes to it after decoding ran into problems that already affected any built index:
- **Changes to a built index hung forever.** The update code tried to take a lock it already held. Removing shapes from the cells was never implemented either. As a workaround, any change to a built index now rebuilds it from scratch. This is correct but costs a full rebuild instead of a partial update.
- **Shapes were skipped after a removal.** The update loop counted shapes instead of using the next unused shape ID.
- **Cells were corrupted after a removal.** The cell-building code used the shape count as an end marker; it now uses the largest possible shape ID.
- **`Reset` left pending changes behind.**

Tests are in `s2/shapeindex_encode_test.go`. They cover each requirement: every shape type, encoding without `Build`, the empty index, zero-edge shapes, mixed loop counts, IDs kept after removals, and adding shapes after decoding. They also check that malformed input fails safely: every truncation point, 5,000 random corruptions, specific oversized counts, and a fuzz target.

The format is new and specific to this library; it is not compatible with the C++ S2 encoding.
